title: Building the room in Blender
author: claude
summary: The whole room was built by a script in Blender, with morning light.
what: We built the complete room with a script: the walls, the glass wall, the floor, the rug, the credenza, the art, the chandelier, the plants and fig, the floor lamp and the curtains. It starts with morning lighting.
why: A script that rebuilds the room from nothing makes every change repeatable, and the user can watch it happen in their open Blender.
how:
We edit the script `build_room.py`, then run it in the user's open Blender through the Blender MCP link ("script, run live"). The script can safely reset the scene each time.

The stand-in table and chairs (the Preview group) are kept out of the baking.
wrong:
- Glass that bends light blocked the sun and sky in Blender, and the room came out black.
- Resetting Blender to its factory settings during a live session breaks the connection to Claude.
fix:
- The windows are now thin see-through glass.
- The chandelier globes are thin glass shells that cast no shadow, lit by small lights inside.
- We never reset Blender to factory settings during a live session.

tech.name: Blender
tech.plain: Free 3D software. We use it to build the room and to calculate how light falls in it.

tech.name: Cycles
tech.plain: Blender's realistic renderer. It follows light the way a camera would see it.

tech.name: Python scripts
tech.plain: Small programs that tell Blender what to build and bake, so every step can be repeated.

tech.name: Blender MCP
tech.plain: A link that lets Claude send commands to the user's open Blender.
